note: Classification of every expected row in qa/scenarios/semantic_v1.json. All labels are team_qa_synthetic proposals written by an AI QA agent from the official checklist and team spec. None is official Ground Truth and none is human-reviewed. Open-item IDs refer to case/CQA_SCORING_SPEC.md section 7.

tiers.deterministic_invariant: Label-free rules checked on every saved output from the checklist, the source transcript and arithmetic alone (see invariants). They need no semantic judgment and no reviewer.
tiers.proposed_unreviewed: One expected response proposed by the QA agent from explicit checklist text. Scored for exact match, but only as an unreviewed proposal until a language-competent human confirms it.
tiers.ambiguous: The official checklist does not establish a unique answer (an open item, or two anchors are defensible). Recorded, never scored.

invariants.statement: The saved conversation equals the source record: same length, and every message keeps its zero-based index, speaker, timestamp and exact text.
Each criterion appears once with a permitted response; N/A only where the criterion defines an N/A condition.
The response is N/A exactly when the model's own applicability atomic answer equals the configured na_when.
The response obeys the checklist consistency rules and, for 01 and 07, the all-of rule over the model's own atomic answers (qa/decision_rules.py).
Every quote is an exact substring of the cited message; scope boundaries exist and are ordered. Formatting-only matches are reported separately.
A positive response cites a quote from a configured role; 01 cites the first human operator reply.
08=no cites the full conversation scope; 08=yes cites an operator quote and categories equal the yes-answered category questions.
The recorded total equals an independent exact-fraction recomputation from the responses and weights.
A counterfactual edit that removes required operator behavior cannot make the target criterion more favorable than on the unedited base conversation.
